subject: Assurance delivery sprint: consolidated pen-test & SBOM traceability
messages:
From: Jason Liu <jason.liu@stratusbank.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: StratusBank InfoSec <infosec@stratusbank.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: consolidated assurance package & traceability for procurement

Hi Logan,

Following up from our intake call earlier this week — procurement and InfoSec have requested a single, consolidated delivery that bundles the high-level pen-test findings (executive summary), SBOM inventory with provenance/hashes, and a clear remediation/patching matrix that maps CVEs to components and expected time-to-remediate. Specifically they want: 

- A one-page executive summary of the recent penetration test (redacted if necessary) and a link to the full report (we understand some details may be redacted for confidentiality).
- SBOM CSV that includes package name, version, source, checksum, and any transitive dependency mapping you can provide (Provenance + build/package IDs).
- Remediation matrix: CVE -> affected package -> first-available-fix -> assigned owner (Redwood) -> target remediation window (e.g., Critical: 7 days, High: 30 days, etc.).
- Formal statement of patch SLAs by severity, and an internal process note on how regressions/reopenings are handled.

Procurement needs this compiled as an "assurance delivery packet" by COB 2026-10-19 to keep the contract timeline intact. Can you confirm Redwood can deliver these artifacts and whether any of the items will need a non-disclosure or redaction agreement?

Thanks,
Jason Liu
Security Risk Manager
StratusBank

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Jason Liu <jason.liu@stratusbank.com>
Cc: StratusBank InfoSec <infosec@stratusbank.com>, priyom_das@redwood.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 15 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: consolidated assurance package & traceability for procurement

Jason — thanks for the clear list. We can assemble that packet and aim to deliver by the 19th. High-level plan below; internal owners CC'd.

Deliverables we will provide (in a single ZIP and a shared Drive folder):
- Pen-test executive summary (PDF) + redacted full report where appropriate. We will include a short note on why items were redacted (third-party NDA, tester notes).
- SBOM inventory CSV with package name, version, source URL, SHA256 checksum, and a provenance column (build-id / container digest).
- Remediation matrix (spreadsheet) mapping CVE -> component -> current version -> fixed version or mitigation -> recommended SLA bucket.
- Patch SLA commitments document (spreadsheet + one-paragraph attestation) describing target windows by severity and escalation path.

Proposed SLA buckets for discussion (we can adjust based on contract needs):
- Critical (RCE/active exploit): 7 business days to mitigation/temporary fix; 30 calendar days for full remediation where applicable.
- High: 30 calendar days.
- Medium: 90 calendar days.
- Low: next regular patch cycle (typically quarterly).

We will provide an explicit field in the remediation matrix identifying whether the fix is a code change, configuration change, or operational mitigator (WAF rule, container config).

Internal assignment: Priyom will own SBOM provenance exports and the mapping to git commits/builds; Stephanie will assemble the remediation matrix and the SLA doc; I will package the artifacts, redact as needed, and transmit to you.

Attachments (stubs):
- 20261015-redwood-pen-test-executive-summary.pdf
- redwood-sbom-inventory-202610.csv
- patch-sla-commitment-202610.xlsx

If you need the full pen-test delivered rather than a redacted copy, please indicate and we'll route for approval with the pen test vendor and legal.

Best,
Logan Wright
Account Executive, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415-555-0182

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Jason Liu <jason.liu@stratusbank.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Oct 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: consolidated assurance package & traceability for procurement

Adding some implementation detail so we match expectations when we package artifacts.

On Thu, Oct 15, 2026 at 11:03 AM Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com> wrote:
> Deliverables we will provide (in a single ZIP and a shared Drive folder):
> - Pen-test executive summary (PDF) + redacted full report where appropriate.
> - SBOM inventory CSV with package name, version, source URL, SHA256 checksum, and a provenance column (build-id / container digest).
> - Remediation matrix (spreadsheet) mapping CVE -> component -> current version -> fixed version or mitigation -> recommended SLA bucket.

I will prepare the SBOM export from our artifact registry and map packages back to the build pipeline metadata (build IDs and container digests). The SBOM CSV draft will include a provenance column with the following format: repo@commit-short | image:digest | build-id. I'll also add a column listing whether the package was pulled from a public registry vs. vendor-provided binary.

For CVE mapping: we have a nightly dependency scanner that links packages to known CVEs and severity scores; I will run an export limited to the deployment images relevant to StratusBank (we keep environment tags). Where a CVE doesn't apply to the deployed runtime (e.g., dev-only library), I'll flag it in the matrix to avoid false positives.

Timeline: I can deliver a SBOM + initial mapping by Mon 2026-10-19 09:00 PDT. Stephanie, would you be able to slot the remediation matrix and SLA doc for close-of-business the same day so we can package and ship?

Cheers,
Priyom
Senior Applied Engineer, RedTeam Tools

From: Jason Liu <jason.liu@stratusbank.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: StratusBank InfoSec <infosec@stratusbank.com>, priyom_das@redwood.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: consolidated assurance package & traceability for procurement

Logan/Priyom/Stephanie — appreciate the quick coordination. That plan works for us; a few final items before we close the loop: 

1) Attestation: Procurement requires a signed attestation (one paragraph) that the SBOM is accurate to the best of Redwood's knowledge and that any redactions are documented. Can you provide a DocuSign-ready document?
2) SLA confirmation: The buckets you proposed look fine. For clarity in contract language we need explicit language for Critical: do you commit to "initial mitigation within 7 business days and full remediation within 30 calendar days where a code change is required"? Please confirm.
3) Separation of concerns: please mark any CVEs in the matrix that will be handled by third-party vendors (e.g., upstream library owners) and indicate whether Redwood will accept the vendor timeline or apply a compensating control.

If you can confirm (1)-(3) and provide the ZIP with the three artifacts to the Drive link below, procurement will proceed with the contracting milestone.

Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aX-example-stratus-assurance
DocuSign: https://docusign.com/envelope/ABC123-STRAT-2026

Thanks again — looking forward to the packet.

Best regards,
Jason Liu
Security Risk Manager
StratusBank
